doc.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023

title: Show business childhood and a musical family
summary: Childhood acquaintances in show business, seeing uncles on TV, mother's stride piano, an uncle arranging at 14, a cousin drumming with Toto.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Wow, where do you go from there?

Where do you go from there? And my childhood acquaintances were Nat King Cole and Judy Garland and the Andrews Sisters and Sophie Tucker, Jack Benny. So without knowing who they were, I was being imbued with this culture of music, you know, show business, music. And it just seemed like a natural thing to me. And then I would see my uncles playing music on television, because they appeared a lot on British T.V. And somewhere it was always, well you know I think I want to do that. It was never any question that I wouldn’t be playing an instrument.
Were your parents on board with that direction they saw you going in?

Oh yeah. I mean my mother played wonderful stride piano which she learned by looking over her brother’s shoulder. And my youngest uncle learned to arrange by looking over his brother’s shoulder. So at the age of 14 he was writing for the Ambrose Band which is quite extraordinary. He was a staff arranger at Lawrence Wright at the age of 14. So there’s a musical gene in the family that runs all the way through to my kids to my cousin
was the drummer with Toto for 30-odd years. You know it’s gone all the way through and carried on which is amazing.
